rv.q: Much like jazz itself, this production is constantly in conversation with the past, building on existing work without trying to neatly resolve it.
There is a palpable and authentic affection for Miles's music underpinning the whole venture.
This is easily one of the finest performances I've witnessed this year.
MILES. is not just a play about Miles Davis, it is a play about all artists who dare to push boundaries, to challenge convention, and to search for truth in their work.

Structurally, the play is more a series of beats or fragments, and weaves together cleverly, something like winding, smoky jazz. Rather than dull out the audience with endless autobiographical detail, we witness a series of moments and emotions, while somehow absorbing the very essence of Miles Davies.

cn.t: Critics warmly embrace this Miles Davis portrait for its authentic affection for the music and standout performances, praising how it captures the boundary-pushing spirit of jazz and artistry without neat resolution.
